_readme: THE GLOBE TEST: the composite Merrimack (scenes/demos/composite_merrimack.json -- the water read from one
product per layer, the height tree under every CPU reader) seen from a globe camera. It starts over the
east coast of North America with the whole planet in view; TAB steps through the views below, each a
globe camera (`at`: lat, lon, heading, tilt, range in metres from the point), from the planet down to
the composite's three regions and the Merrimack's mouth. The instant is fixed, so a still repeats.
KEYS   TAB the next view   G the debug views (wire, flat, edges, normals, height, depth, meshlets,
albedo, residency of colour / height / land-sea)   mouse drag turns the globe, wheel zooms
Make the products first (network once, cached after):
dotnet run --project harvest/harvest -- compose-water --fidelity harvest/testdata/coast3_3to10m.gafid --out data/composite/coast3
THE PLANET'S BUILDINGS AND ROADS (2026-10-15): the same folded tree the earth scene draws (docs/BUILDING_LOD.md,
docs/ROADS.md section 5), so the coast folds up into its towns as the views step down. The layer and its
sources are the earth scene's, merged by name over the composite base (the named-array law).
THE NAMED-ARRAY LAW REACHED `sources` ON 2026-10-18: until then a scene's sources REPLACED its base's, so this
scene had none of the place's imagery (the land at the Merrimack was Google at the cache's zoom: Mark's 'why
does the land look low res'). It now inherits the MassGIS orthos, the highlights and the ETOPO ring, and drops
the composite scene's water.bed by name: with its five file-backed rungs in the height stack a height page
cost 3.5 s through the stack's direct readers (824 loads, 53,003 window decodes, the land unpainted after
3,000 frames); without them the same eye settles exact in 659 frames at 13.8 ms a load (CONTENT_SCALING
section 4; the reader is open in its section 5).
